title: What is Data in ML? 🗂️
description: Understand observations, features, and labels – the building blocks of any dataset.

slides.title: Data = Experience 📖
slides.content:
# The Foundation of Learning

Machine learning models don’t have life experience — they learn from **data**. Every row, every column, every number is a lesson.

Think of a dataset as a **spreadsheet**:
- **Rows** → observations, examples, instances.
- **Columns** → features (attributes) and optionally **labels** (what we want to predict).

An observation might be one house, one customer, one image.

slides.title: Features vs. Labels 🏷️
slides.content:
# Input and Output

- **Features**: the known information we use to make predictions. For a house: number of bedrooms, area, location.
- **Labels**: the target we want to predict. e.g., sale price.

In supervised learning, every row has both features and a label. In unsupervised learning, we only have features — the model must find patterns without a label.

💡 *Labels are also called targets, dependent variables, or y. Features are independent variables or X.*

quizData.question: In a dataset of used cars, which of these would typically be a feature?
quizData.explanation: Mileage is an attribute you have before prediction; it's a feature. Resale value would be the label if you're trying to predict it.

slides.title: A Tiny Dataset 🐍
slides.content: Here’s how a simple housing dataset might look in Python using pandas:
slides.codeSnippet:
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'area_sqft': [1500, 800, 2200],
    'bedrooms': [3, 2, 4],
    'price': [300000, 180000, 500000]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df.head())

slides.title: Why Quality Data Matters 💎
slides.content:
# Garbage In, Garbage Out

If your data is messy, missing, or biased, even the smartest algorithm will produce poor results.

- **Missing values** confuse the math.
- **Outliers** can distort patterns.
- **Inconsistent formats** break training.

Spending 80% of your time on data preparation is normal. The model is just the tip of the iceberg.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Think Like a Detective
Before you code, ask: *What story does this data tell? What could go wrong?* A curious mindset is your best tool.
